identifier: Setting up your Shopify Payments account
statement: Your Shopify Payments payouts might be placed on hold until two-step authentication is activated on your store.

identifier: Setting up your Shopify Payments account
statement: You need to choose your store currency before making your first sale. It’s the currency that will be used throughout your Shopify admin, for pricing your products and viewing your reports. If you need to change your store currency after making your first sale, then contact Shopify Support.
In the Shopify Payments section, click Activate Shopify Payments
Enter the required personal, address, and identification information, and then click Next
Enter the required information about your business.
Enter the phone number that you want to display on your customer's bank statement, and then click Next
Click Submit for verification

identifier: Switch to Shopify Payments, Staff permissions
statement: Only the store owner can activate or switch to Shopify Payments. Staff members can't switch to Shopify Payments.
After your account verification is complete, click Activate
After your Shopify Payments account is verified, you can connect your bank account in the Payments section of your Shopify admin to receive payouts.
If bank account ownership verification is required, then follow the instructions in your Shopify admin.

Some local payment methods for Shopify Payments require additional approval before they can be activated. Once you activate Shopify Payments, the review process for applicable local payment methods begins automatically and approved payment methods will become available for you to activate in the payment methods page.

Shopify and its banking partners are required to collect and verify information about you and your business, to comply with regulations that are designed to prevent financial crimes. As local rules and regulations evolve, you might be contacted by Shopify and its banking partners to provide additional information throughout the lifespan of your Shopify Payments account.
The information that is collected is used to confirm the identity of the business, the identities of individuals linked to it, and the nature of the relationship between the two.

identifier: Uploading documents for Shopify Payments verification, Note
statement: Once documentation is uploaded, it can take up to 24 hours to be reviewed. Your Shopify Payments account status will show the submission as "pending" until a response is received.

identifier: Uploading documents for Shopify Payments verification
statement: Due to the sensitive nature of the personal information that's requested, Shopify can only accept documents that are uploaded through the secure banners in your Shopify admin. For your security and privacy, any documents sent through email or support chat are redacted and rendered unusable.

identifier: Uploading documents for Shopify Payments verification
statement: * The documentation is photographed instead of scanned, copied, or screenshotted. Ensure photographs are in color and not grayscale. * For documents that are issued to you digitally, you must provide the original PDF without any alterations, and with all original pages included. * The documentation is clear enough to read, with all four borders of the document in the frame. * The documentation is complete with all details visible and nothing censored, blurred, or cropped out. * The information on your documentation matches the information that you entered on your Shopify Payments account.

identifier: Uploading documents for Shopify Payments verification
statement: Your Shopify Payments payouts might be placed on hold until your information and documents can be verified. If documentation is required, then an alert is sent to notify you and take you to the upload page where you can provide new information.

identifier: Uploading documents for Shopify Payments verification
statement: When you upload documents for Shopify Payments verification or you try to update your Shopify Payments details, you might receive an error message indicating that you've reached the maximum number of attempts. If this happens, then you can contact Shopify Support to make further changes to your details or to submit additional documents.

identifier: Common reasons a document isn't verified
statement: Your account details and your documents must match.

Every Shopify Payments account must list one individual as the account representative, even when the business is a registered company or is owned by another company. Shopify's banking partners require identity information for a real person on every account, so you can't list a company as the account representative.

* **Individuals and sole proprietorships**: The person who owns and operates the business. * **All other business types**: An owner or a senior executive who has the authority to legally bind the business to the Shopify Payments Terms of Service.

Businesses where no individual owns 25% or more, such as publicly traded companies, government entities, and non-profits, still need to name an account representative. This requirement comes from banking regulations and can't be waived.

identifier: Understanding the terms Owner, Director and Executive
statement: For most regions, owners are defined as any individual person who directly or indirectly (through ownership in a parent or holding company) owns 25% or more of the business’s equity. If there are individuals who own equity of your business through their ownership of the holding company, then you must list them as beneficial owners.
You can't use PO Box or Private Mail Box addresses with Shopify Payments.

If your business is based in the United States, and you want to use Shopify Balance or Shopify Credit, then you're unable to use virtual addresses, mail forwarding services, co-working spaces, registering agent addresses, or similar addresses which your business might use on documentation, but doesn't physically occupy. To use these products and services, you must provide the real home addresses for the people on file, and a business address where your business operations can be physically located.
scope: If your business is based in the United States

statement: Everyone listed on your Shopify Payments account should provide the full legal name that is displayed on their government-issued photo ID or documentation. Don't use nicknames, abbreviations, aliases, or placeholders, such as Admin or Manager. Don't use numeric characters or asterisks in a name.

During your free trial, your online store is automatically in private mode. In private mode, your site's pages are inaccessible, and a customizable landing page with a password option is displayed instead.

Before you can launch your store, you must complete the following required steps: * Select a subscription plan. If you pick a plan during a free trial, then you won't be charged any subscription fees until your free trial expires. * Add a store address to the **Business details** section of the **Settings** > **General** page. * Set up a payment method, and make sure that test mode is deactivated.
If you want your store to be displayed in the Shop app, then launching your store is one of the Shop merchant requirements
After you launch your store, it can take up to 48 hours for your Shop eligibility status to update.

identifier: Launch your store from Online Store > Preferences
statement: In the Store access section, deactivate the Private mode setting.

identifier: Setting up your store during the free trial
statement: When you open a store on a free trial, your store is initially in private mode, or its checkout is inactive.

identifier: Setting up your store during the free trial
statement: To allow customers to purchase products, you can either deactivate private mode, or you can activate your online store checkout, and POS in-person sales if applicable, by choosing a paid plan.

identifier: Setting up your store during the free trial
statement: To sell and accept orders during your free trial, you need to set up a payment provider.
When you're ready to start selling products, you need to select a paid plan.

identifier: Choosing a paid plan, Store activation
statement: **Store activation**: After you choose a paid plan, your online store's checkout, and POS in-person sales if applicable, are activated.

identifier: Choosing a paid plan, Trial expiry
statement: **Trial expiry**: If you don't select a monthly plan at the end of your free trial, then your store is paused until you choose a paid plan.

identifier: After the promotional pricing period ends
statement: After your promotional pricing period ends, you need to select a standard-rate plan to continue using Shopify. If you don't select a plan, then your store might be frozen until you choose one.

identifier: Options if you're not ready to launch or build, Pause your store
statement: **Pause your store**: You can pause your store at a reduced monthly rate. Customers can still view your products, but checkout is deactivated.

identifier: Troubleshoot store paused after trial ends
statement: If your free trial ends before you choose a paid plan, then your store is automatically paused. To resume selling, log in to your Shopify admin and select a paid plan. Your store data, products, and settings are preserved.
The requirement for a Proof of Liveness check for Shopify Payments is based on your country.

To complete a Proof of Liveness check, you’ll use your webcam or phone to upload a selfie. You also need to verify your photo ID using one of the following methods: * Use your webcam or phone to take a photo of your ID document. * Upload a photo of your ID document.

Only the account owner can complete a Liveness check and photo ID verification. This check is necessary to complete the Shopify Payments setup process and ensure that your store can process transactions using Shopify Payments.
If your store is flagged for review and is temporarily unavailable, then Shopify sends an email to the store owner's email address.
To submit an appeal, log in to your Shopify admin, where you're redirected to the appeal form. If you use Shopify Payments, then your account is temporarily suspended during the review.

identifier: Handling a Shopify store review, Caution
statement: If you don't submit your appeal within 3 consecutive days of receiving the email notification from Shopify, then your store will be terminated

identifier: Reasons for a Shopify store review
statement: Stores are flagged for review only when there are serious concerns about compliance with these terms.

identifier: Submitting an appeal for your store, Steps
statement: On the appeal form, complete the following actions: * Provide information about your business. * Upload a valid government-issued ID. * Optional: Submit extra documentation or other details about your business, such as proof of business association and proof of inventory.
To sell products using the Shopify platform, you must comply with the laws of the jurisdiction of your business and your customers, the Shopify Terms of Service

identifier: Laws and regulations for selling alcohol in the United States (US)
statement: If your business is located in the United States, or if you sell alcohol products to customers in the United States, then you're required to follow all federal, state, and local laws in any jurisdiction where your alcohol products are advertised or sold.
scope: If your business is located in the United States, or if you sell alcohol products to customers in the United States

identifier: Laws and regulations for selling alcohol in the United States (US)
statement: * Acquire and maintain all necessary licenses individually to produce, market, sell, and deliver your products. * Remain in full compliance with all applicable license requirements, including record-keeping requirements. * Have effective age verification practices so that alcohol products can't be purchased or received by people who are under the age of 21. * Ship and deliver alcohol products in full compliance with applicable laws of the jurisdiction of your business and your customers' jurisdiction. If you ship to a different state, then you must comply with that state’s laws.

identifier: Requirements for selling hemp and hemp-derived products in the United States (US)
statement: To sell hemp and hemp-derived products containing cannabidiol (CBD) on Shopify in the United States (US), you must ensure that you comply with the requirements described on this page.

identifier: Hemp and hemp-derived product compliance statements, I confirm that:
statement: 1. I am the account owner or business owner and have authority to bind my business to these statements. My business will follow these rules as long as it sells, or offers to sell, hemp and hemp-derived products. 2. The address listed in my Shopify admin matches the state from which I conduct my business. 3. My Shopify store operates from a jurisdiction where the online listing and sale of hemp and hemp-derived products is permitted by applicable federal, state, and local laws. I have all of the applicable state and local licenses, approvals, and certifications required to sell hemp and hemp-derived products in the US. 4. I will notify Shopify in writing to legal@shopify.com of any class action demand letter or Food and Drug Administration (FDA) or Federal Trade Commission (FTC) enforcement action commenced against my business, including any warning letters or other related correspondence within ten days of receipt. 5. Any time Shopify requests, I will provide documentation that confirms that my Shopify store, business, and cannabis products are in compliance with laws, regulations, and any of the requirements outlined here.

identifier: Compliance requirements for hemp and hemp-derived products, I confirm that for all hemp and hemp-derived products listed or sold on my Shopify store:
statement: 1. Those products don't contain more than 0.3% tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) concentration on a dry weight basis or such lower percentage as required by applicable state and local law. 2. Those products have been sourced, processed, tested, labeled and marketed in compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws. 3. Those products are legal in every jurisdiction into which they're sold, including jurisdictions outside the US, as applicable.

identifier: Compliance requirements for hemp and hemp-derived products
statement: 4. Those products have been sourced, processed, tested, labeled, and marketed as required by federal, state, and local law. 5. Those products aren't marketed as having any medicinal, disease-related, or therapeutic benefit, or any other marketing claims unless such claims have been approved by the FDA for that specific product category such as cosmetics or dietary supplements. 6. Those products have not been the subject of a recall or safety alert from an applicable regulatory authority. In the event of a recall or safety alert, I confirm that I will immediately remove the applicable product(s) from my Shopify store and stop fulfilling, processing, or receiving orders for such products.

identifier: Compliance requirements for hemp and hemp-derived products
statement: I understand that if I fail to comply with the confirmations and promises here, or if Shopify determines in its sole discretion that further action is required, that Shopify may take action against my account, up to and including store termination.

identifier: American Express requirements for Shopify Payments
statement: American Express sets its own requirements for the addresses and the names recorded on a payment account. These requirements apply to your Shopify Payments account in addition to the general Shopify Payments eligibility requirements.

identifier: American Express requirements for Shopify Payments
statement: If a detail on your account doesn't meet these requirements, then American Express stops being available at checkout in your store. Your store keeps accepting other card brands throughout. In some cases you're contacted by Shopify Trust teams and asked to make the update by a specific date instead. American Express stays available at checkout until that date passes.
American Express doesn't accept a post office (PO) box or a private mailbox as an address on a payment account. These can't be used as a business address or as a residential address.

The first and last names of the people that are listed on your account must be their complete legal names, and must meet all of the following conditions: * Each name is at least 2 characters long. * The first name and the last name are different from each other. * Neither name is made up of the same character repeated, such as a name entered as AAAA. * Neither name contains a number. * Neither name is a placeholder word, such as Admin, Manager, Merchant, or Owner. * Neither name contains an asterisk.

identifier: When bank account ownership verification is required
statement: Bank account ownership verification might be required when you add or replace a payout bank account for Shopify Payments. You might also be asked to verify your bank account again if your Shopify Payments business details change.

identifier: When bank account ownership verification is required
statement: Verification compares the name on your bank account with information on your Shopify Payments account. This information can include your legal business name or account representative name.

Your bank statement must be clear, complete, uncropped, and issued within the last 6 months. It must display the following information: * Account holder name * Bank account details, such as account number, International Bank Account Number (IBAN), routing number, or sort code * Bank name * Issue date

If bank account ownership verification isn't complete, then a banner in your Shopify admin explains the issue and any required action. Follow the action in the banner, such as **Upload document** or **update your business details**. Some Shopify Payments payouts might be paused until the issue is resolved.

identifier: Shopify Payments account verification updates in Europe and the United Kingdom
statement: Verification requirements for Shopify Payments accounts in Europe and the United Kingdom (UK) are being updated throughout 2026. These updates align with local financial regulations, including requirements from the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI).
Only the store owner can view and complete verification requests for Shopify Payments accounts. Staff members don't have access to the verification request page.

Periodic re-verification is a normal part of using Shopify Payments. Verification requirements from financial partners and card networks evolve over time, which means you might be asked to confirm or update information even if nothing about your business has changed.

Ownership information on file is compared against your government business registry. Any person that is listed on your registry as owning 25% or more equity must be listed on your Shopify Payments account with the **Owner** role.
scope: supported European countries and territories, and the United Kingdom

statement: If your store is based in the UK and your business has beneficial owners, then you must verify both the beneficial owners and the directors. Anyone that is listed on your business's registry as a director must be listed on your Shopify Payments account with the **Director** role.
scope: If your store is based in the UK

statement: If you don't complete a verification request by the deadline displayed in your Shopify admin, then your payouts are temporarily paused until verification is complete. If your payouts are paused, then a second deadline might be displayed for when your ability to accept orders through Shopify Payments is also paused.

statement: Both pauses are temporary and are lifted automatically after you complete verification.

statement: If you created your Shopify Payments account in or after June 2026, then you must complete verification to receive payouts and to continue processing payments. Your payouts are paused until you complete verification, and if verification isn't complete within 90 days of your first Shopify Payments order, then payments are refunded to your customers.

statement: - Your payouts are paused immediately. - Your charges are paused 30 days after your first Shopify Payments order. - Payments processed through Shopify Payments are refunded to your customers 90 days after your first Shopify Payments order.

statement: Payments processed using payment providers other than Shopify Payments aren't affected.
